_note: How the game LOOKS and FEELS: animation, hit effects, particles, UI motion and backgrounds. Nothing here changes the rules or balance. Times are in seconds, sizes in screen pixels unless they say tiles. Set a strength to 0 to switch an effect off.

characters._note: The animals. How big each is drawn in battle, and how big any may look on the screen, is bodies.json (sprite_scale here is only the arena crowd's, arena_life.gd). class_badge_radius: the class icon under each one, in pixels. shader_enabled false is the lighter option for slow phones (no shader at all; hits flash with a plain tint). shader_* values drive the per-animal shader (scripts/fx/unit.gdshader): a soft warm highlight on the edge facing the light (top-left), a soft cool rim light on the far edge (both edge_width texels wide at 56 pixels a tile, following the smooth edge so they stay smooth at any zoom), a little extra color punch, and gentle volume (gradient). The outline is the render's own single deep line; shader_line_tint above 0 tints it toward a dark shade (line_darkness) of the body color. In battle, team_outline_texels: a bold band in the team's color (blue yours, red the enemy's) round each sprite, this many texels wide (0: none; 3D models: "models" team_outline_px).

combat._note: Combat juice. A hit squashes the animal hit_squash and shoves it hit_knockback_pixels, adding up for hits close together but never past hit_squash_max and hit_knockback_max_pixels. Every hit shows when it lands: the attacker's wind-up plays first (started then if none was showing) and a shot flies (shot_tiles_per_second, between shot_min_seconds and shot_max_seconds), and only then do the flash, sparks, number and health-bar drop show; a defeat follows its last hit by defeat_after_hit_seconds. Each attack starts up to impact_jitter_seconds later than it could (0: armies strike in unison); a hit that comes within strike_grace_seconds of a strike lands on that strike. Health bars show once an animal is hurt and fade away (over health_bar_fade_seconds) when it hasn't been hit for health_bar_hide_after seconds. Strong hits (at least strong_hit_pct of the target's health, a charge, a pounce or a dive) flash, squash and knock back harder; only big hits (big_hit_pct) and knockouts pause the whole fight for a moment (hit-stop, at most once every hitstop_cooldown) and shake it. Shake is in pixels. A strike lunges the body lunge_pixels toward its target (classes more or less), but never further than lunge_gap_share of the gap to the target's body (bodies.json footprint; under half, so two striking at once just meet): a strike reaches with jaws and paws, not by moving the body into the target.

movement._note: How animals move on screen. Only the drawing: where an animal is in the fight never changes. It follows its place in the fight like a spring (follow_rate, higher = snappier; each animal's may differ by up to follow_variety, 0 in armies so ranks move as one; through a swing it holds its ground, as the fight itself holds it (battle_rules.json swing): the walking the fight does for it waits until the swing is done, pushes and knockbacks still move it), easing into and out of a run, and may wander up to march_wobble_tiles while marching (about every march_wobble_seconds; 0: armies march in step). Animals fighting are nudged apart on screen until their pictures are spread_body_share of their height apart (enemies in a scrap spread_enemy_share of that, a flier over an animal on the ground spread_air_share; one straight behind another also steps aside by spread_sideways, so a line staggers), at spread_rate, by at most spread_max_tiles, drifting back at spread_return_rate once there's room. They face exactly where their body in the fight faces (battle_rules.json spacing turn_degrees_per_tick: at what it strikes or the way it goes, a push never turns it), blended between fight ticks; an animal with no fight behind it (the animation preview) turns at turn_degrees_per_second. A sprite switches to the next of its 8 drawn directions only once turn_hysteresis_degrees past halfway, and pinches a little (turn_squash, for turn_squash_seconds) as it does. They walk only when moving on their own faster than walk_min_speed_tiles a second (for at least walk_hold_seconds); the walk plays as fast as the feet cover the ground (walk_stride_match 1 = exactly; a marching army's too, each animal at its own stride), kept between walk_min_fps and walk_max_fps. Stopping gives a small settling bounce (arrive_squash).

acting._note: How animals act, on top of their rendered animations. Each plays its idle and walk at its own pace (up to pace_variety faster or slower). It blinks (blink_seconds, every blink_every seconds) and, standing about with nothing in reach, fidgets now and then (fidget_every; the first after fidget_first). Faces drawn over the eyes: a squint on the wind-up, wide eyes for wide_seconds when hit, dizzy swirls when stunned or knocked out, drowsy lids when slowed, happy eyes when celebrating, a smug look for smug_seconds after a knockout. A hit makes it flinch (flinch_degrees) and bounce (hurt_bounce_pixels over hurt_seconds). A sprite's change of animation squashes it a little (transition_squash); a 3D model cross-fades into its next animation over blend_seconds instead (no hard cuts). A 3D model's own animation moves its body (its steps, its wind-up and strike), so the cartoon squash and stretch, the walk's hops and the breathing (characters, combat) play on a model at model_squash_share of their size: a touch of squash and stretch, its height never pumping with each step and swing (a hit's squash stays full), and however it squashes and stretches it never stands more than model_stretch_max taller than itself (the camera keeps every animal's tallest pose under bodies.json limits with little to spare). A swing always plays at its own pace, every one the same (windup_scale, stun_windup_scale and slow_windup_scale are 1: how often an animal hits is the pause between swings, never a faster or slower swing). Classes move their own way: Tanks plod (tank_hop of the walk's hop) with a thump and dust at each step (tank_step_squash); Tank Destroyers lean in (td_lean), crouch and spring at a pounce (td_pounce_pixels) and lunge further (td_lunge); Ranged kick back on every shot (ranged_recoil_pixels); fliers fly air_height_tiles above the ground (a real height: they pass over the animals under them and never through them, and sort in front of or behind them rightly), bob (air_bob_pixels at air_bob_speed), swoop (air_swoop_pixels), bank into turns (air_bank_degrees), rise before a dive (air_dive_rise_pixels) and drop into it (air_dive_drop_pixels). The winners celebrate for victory_seconds with bounces of victory_hop_pixels. A knockout poofs, or (defeat_fling_chance) bounces off the screen with a spin over defeat_fling_seconds. Stunned animals wobble (stun_wobble_degrees); slowed ones move at slow_pace with a Zzz every zzz_every seconds. Below sweat_below of their health they sweat (a drop every sweat_every seconds). Setting off, one may trip (trip_chance, for trip_seconds, at most once every trip_cooldown seconds). Specialist traits act too: a Stun animal's stunning blow comes after its rendered wind-up (a chest beat, a hiss, a roar) or, without one, a trembling stare stretching the wind-up by stun_windup_scale; a Slow animal's wind-up is a lazy yawn, slow_windup_scale as long, with drowsy eyes; a Splash animal rises splash_hop_pixels for a belly flop and lands squashed (splash_squash); a Burrow animal sinks into the ground over dig_seconds and pops out with a springy boing over emerge_seconds (emerge_hop_pixels high). Body plans walk their own way: fish wiggle (fish_wiggle_degrees), upright animals waddle (waddle_degrees), snakes ripple, frogs bound, seals and whales slide, shrimp scuttle.

choreography._note: How a fight is staged. It opens with a beat of intro_seconds: both herds hop into place (intro_hop_pixels high, spread over intro_hop_spread_seconds) and a bouncy FIGHT! banner (fight_banner_size) shows before the fight starts. When stall_animals or fewer are left and nobody has been knocked out for stall_after_seconds, the fight gradually plays faster, up to stall_max_speed after stall_ramp_seconds more (only how fast it plays, never what happens). The last knockout plays in slow motion (final_slow_motion) with a push-in (final_zoom, in over final_zoom_in_seconds, held until final_hold_seconds after the knockout, out over final_zoom_out_seconds; never so far that an animal looks bigger than bodies.json limits allow, so in a small fight it may barely push in); then the winners celebrate and the score shows.

effects._note: Particles. max_particles caps how many can be on screen at once (lower it on slow phones).

crowd._note: Keeping big fights readable and smooth. A fight is crowded from crowded_from_units animals on the field: bursts use particles_when_crowded of their particles, ordinary hits lose their claw and bite marks, fewer sparks and numbers show, and (plain_animals_when_crowded) the animals skip their shader so many of a kind draw together; that look is chosen as the herds come on, not mid-fight. Hit sparks: at most hit_sparks_max bursts at once (hit_sparks_when_crowded when crowded), each counting for spark_seconds; when that many are showing, a bigger hit takes the place of the smallest. Damage numbers work the same way (combat number_max_on_screen; numbers_when_crowded when crowded). Hit-stop pauses come at most once every hitstop_cooldown_when_crowded (a crowded fight has a knockout every moment). Busy spots, in any fight: where at least busy_from_units animals stand within a square busy_cell_tiles across and the eight round it, only big hits (combat big_hit_pct) and knockouts always show their sparks and number; a strong hit (strong_hit_pct) shows while fewer than busy_numbers_max numbers are up in that spot; anything smaller keeps quiet: no sparks or claw marks, and no new damage number (it adds to one already showing on that animal, without making it pop again). A quiet hit still flashes and drops the health bar; the defeat poofs, shots and everything else show as ever.

models._note: The animals as real 3D models in battle (scripts/fx/model_stage.gd, art/models/battle/) instead of sprites. enabled: on everywhere: fights, the army while picking, the arena previews (off: the older sprites; Developer tools > Big army test (sprites) compares). render_scale_max: at most this many real pixels per layout pixel; msaa: antialiasing (0, 2 or 4); outline_px: the dark outline's width at one real pixel per layout pixel. In battle, a bold band in the team's color (blue yours, red the enemy's) team_outline_px wide sits outside the dark outline, so sides read at a glance even packed close (0: none); it's a second hull pushed team_outline_depth tiles back so the dark line stays on top. Shading is the 3D viewer's (viewer.json "look").

camera._note: The fight's camera. When the field grows for bigger herds (draft_rules.json "field"), the camera zooms out to it over about zoom_seconds. When the view already reaches the far fence (the line-up, a fight at the back), it eases on past it by up to scenery_back_tiles so the crowd behind the fence shows (data/arena_life.json); from scenery_reach_tiles away it doesn't. tilt_degrees: how far the battle camera leans from looking straight down (0: top-down; 40: it looks down at 50 degrees from level, as the sprites were drawn). The 3D animals, the arena pictures (tools/creatures/arena.py) and anything lifted off the ground (fliers' height) use it; the ground itself keeps square tiles on the screen at any tilt (the field is stretched to match).

celebrations._note: Big moments. After each fight the new score pops up over the field (score_pop_size) and flies into the score bar. A 3-star animal gets a slow-motion zoom (zoom in, hold, zoom out, with the field's animation slowed by star3_slow_motion; never so far that an animal looks bigger than bodies.json limits allow), stars, confetti and a bouncy 3 STARS!, then keeps a gold glow (gold_glow) with a sparkle every gold_sparkle_seconds. Flawless: winning a round without losing an animal. Comeback Victory: winning the match after being 2 rounds down.

rivals._note: Rival Rangers. The VS screen before a match (versus_seconds before it goes on by itself, 0 to wait for a tap; it can't be tapped away before versus_min_seconds), and the rival's emote bubbles in the match (shown for emote_seconds, at most one every emote_gap_seconds). Beating a boss plays its celebration for boss_celebration_seconds before the result shows.

ui._note: Buttons and tappable cards squash when pressed and spring back with an overshoot (big panels squash less); popups and the Draft Duel panel pop in. Numbers in pills tick to their new value over count_seconds; short messages over the field stay for toast_seconds. A tap shows tap_sparkles sparkles; the main button on a screen breathes (breathe_amount, breathe_seconds); brass and gold icons catch a glint every glint_seconds; shop cards bob gently (card_bob_pixels, card_bob_seconds) and pop in stagger_seconds apart; a bought card flies to your herd (fly_seconds, along an arc fly_arc_pixels high) and lands with a squash (land_squash) and land_puffs puffs of dust.

pick._note: The Pick 3 screen. Card sizes are [width, height] in game pixels: offer_card for the options after round 1 (four animals in one tray, animal_tray, and two tools in another below it, tool_tray, each tray tray_padding pixels round its cards), start_card for round 1's collection grid, herd_card for your army row; choice_button for the Upgrade and +Squad buttons you get by tapping an animal in your army; army_height: how tall your army in formation is drawn while picking at least (it takes the room the options leave; framed with army_margin_tiles around it, at least army_min_tiles across, zoomed in up to army_max_zoom); slot_size for the three pick slots, undo_badge for the back arrow on your latest pick. Holding a card shows its info (see info). After a fight, the result shows for result_seconds before the next round's picks. The opponent takes between the two bot_pick_seconds over each pick.

bans._note: The ban screen before a match (scripts/ui/ban_screen.gd). card: [width, height] of each animal card in the grid (columns across). The coin flip spins for coin_seconds. The rival thinks for between the two think_seconds before each ban (dots bouncing by its face). A ban stamps a big red X on the card: it drops in over stamp_seconds from stamp_scale times its size, with a shake of stamp_shake pixels. After the last ban, the screen waits done_seconds and goes on to your deck.

transition._note: Changing screens: a leafy circle closes (cover_seconds) with a swirl of leaves, then opens on the next screen (reveal_seconds).

background._note: The arena behind the fight, in its full painted colors (arena_saturation 1 = as painted; the animals stand out by their dark outlines and bold colors), with gentle motion.

styles._note: How the animals' attack styles look (fx/style_look.gd on the animal, battle_field.gd for the moments; the rules are styles.json). The Brown Bear's swipe draws one wide arc across both targets for sweep_seconds. The Yeti glows frost the hit before its ground pound, which rings out in frost and shakes the field pound_shake. The turtle's shell is shell_width of its height across. A shot the Elephant takes for a teammate flashes a shield for shield_seconds. Colors for each. A Wild Boar's or Tiger's big first hit shakes the field slam_shake; Cerberus's three bites land bite_stagger_seconds apart. The Raccoon's trash flies lob_arc times higher and lob_flight times longer; the Cobra's shots take sniper_flight of the time, flat; the Camel's spit is spit_scale times as big; the Squirrel's pinecones are pellet_scale of a nut, pellet_stagger_seconds apart; the Orangutan's fruit bounces on bounce_seconds after it lands. Profile > Developer tools > Attack styles starts each animal's little fight over every showcase_seconds, its enemies biting at showcase_enemy_bite_pct; Slow plays it at showcase_slow_speed. The Falcon rises climb_pixels as it climbs away from a dive, stretched out with speed lines as it dives; the Owl leaves a ghostly owl_trail; the Harpy Eagle flies carry_lift of its height higher with its catch dangling below; a cracked animal shows a crack mark for as long as it lasts; the Condor grows feast_grow bigger for every fall it feasts on (but never past bodies.json limits: it grows into the room they leave it at the camera's zoom), a wisp flying into it over feast_seconds; the Dragon's burning line sweeps out over fire_reveal_seconds and flickers until it goes out. Specialists: the Pangolin curls into a scaly ball (scales colors), a flipped Tank lies upside down; the Seal flattens out on a slide with water streaks; the Kraken's tentacles (tentacle) reach out and slam, tentacle_stagger_seconds apart; the Eel's lightning (lightning) jumps from one to the next, crackling the hit before; the Gorilla's shockwave (shock) shakes the field shock_shake; the Red Panda rears up tall (panda ring); the Sloth's slow-motion zone (zone) is drawn on the ground round it, and shots into it take crawl_flight times as long.
styles._mythics: The Mythics' upgrades on screen. The Yeti's pound rings out as a layered ice blast (fx_layer "ice_blast", ice_blast_seconds long and ice_blast_reach of the pound's radius): a white core flash (ice_core), an icy glow (frost), a shockwave ring, ice_shards shards bursting up out of the ground (ice_dark edges), ice_cracks frost cracks across it, snow_puffs puffs of snow (snow) and a shake (pound_shake); the hit before a pound, frost gathers onto its fists (sparkles every gather_every seconds drawn in from gather_radius of its height round a point gather_height up); its frost patch (frost_patch) stays behind, and an enemy frozen on it gets a smaller burst and a block of ice; Cerberus's lit heads blazing and its fire breath (fire_breath_seconds); burning animals licked by flames; the Unicorn's healing sparkles (heal_sparkle); an animal panicked by the Dragon's fire shaking with sweat (sweat), a "!" in panic_color; the Kraken's ink cloud (ink, ink_puffs puffs swirling in it) and inked animals dripping, a blinded Ranged or Air animal with ink over its eyes and a "?"; a blinded shot fizzles (blind_puff).

army._note: How armies look (Draft Duel). A formation marches with a thump (stomp_volume_db) and a tiny shake (stomp_shake) every march_stride_tiles of ground it covers; each animal's feet keep pace with the ground it covers at its own stride (feel.json movement walk_*; no sliding), and small random differences are kept only for standing about (breathing, fidgets, blinks, expressions). Every animal is drawn at its bodies.json size; an elite Specialist elite_scale bigger. Before a fight the armies stand in formation for lineup_seconds, then FIGHT!. The camera frames every animal still standing with camera_margin_tiles around them (and camera_head_room_tiles more above, for their heads and banners) (never closer than camera_min_tiles across or camera_max_zoom, nor so close that an animal looks bigger than bodies.json "limits" allows), easing over camera_seconds. Squad banners: a flag banner_width x banner_height pixels on a banner_pole pixels pole, at banner_alpha; once the armies are at war (the melee) they fade to banner_war_alpha over banner_fade_seconds, so the fighting animals under them read clearly (a tapped squad's shows in full). Volleys fly slower and higher than single shots (volley_tiles_per_second, between volley_min_seconds and volley_max_seconds, volley_arc times the usual arc). Every other shot in an army fight flies at least over_allies_arc times the usual arc, so it plainly goes over the teammates in between. The clash shakes the field (clash_shake) and freezes it for clash_hitstop_seconds; the War Horn shakes it war_horn_shake. While picking, new squads march in from walk_in_tiles behind the army at walk_in_tiles_per_second (walk_in_steps_per_second steps). Once the armies are at war the camera frames where the fighting is: the animals with an enemy within camera_fight_reach_tiles (edge to edge), at most camera_fight_max_tiles across round the middle of the fighting, so it tightens in as they clash; during the line-up and the march it frames everyone.

readability._note: Telling who's doing what in a fight. When an animal turns on an enemy biting it up close (the targeting rules' threat response, battle_rules.json "targeting"), a cartoon "!" pops over its head for alert_seconds: alert_size pixels tall, alert_color, popping in with alert_pop overshoot. Not shown for ordinary target changes. Who's shooting at whom: every shot trails a streak in the shooter's team color (blue yours, red the enemy's) over the last shot_trail_seconds of its flight, up to shot_trail_width pixels wide and shot_trail_alpha strong, with a ring of it shot_ring_scale times the shot's size (shot_ring_px wide) round the shot, and its landing sparks take the team color too. The animals' own team bands: "models" team_outline_px (3D) and "characters" team_outline_texels (sprites). Seeing what a squad is doing: a quick tap on its banner (within squad_banner_tap_px) or one of its animals picks it (the same again, or a tap on nothing, lets go; a hold still shows info, and a tool being aimed takes the tap). Its animals glow on the ground (squad_glow_alpha strong, squad_glow_scale times their size, pulsing at squad_pulse_speed) and their 3D band grows squad_band_boost_px wider and brighter; its flag gets a ring; for squad_lines_seconds, dashed lines (squad_line_px wide, squad_dash_px dashes) run from each to the enemy it's going for, with a target ring (squad_marker_px) on that enemy. The fight never pauses or slows for it.

card_show._note: How much a card shows off, by rarity (scripts/ui/card_show.gd; its colors are in ui_style.json, show_*). Common: plain. Rare: a soft shine on the frame, a bright line round its inside edge and a glint on top (glint: its size in card-widths), all still, so it costs nothing. Epic: a band of light sweeping across the picture every sweep_seconds (sweep_share of the time, sweep_alpha strong), and a soft glow. Legendary: a glowing edge pulsing every pulse_seconds, and sparkles drifting off the top and sides of the frame (each lives sparkle_seconds and drifts drift card-widths). Mythic: the rose pink frame with its rainbow sheen (rainbow: how far the rim's color drifts toward a turning rainbow, rainbow_seconds per turn), a shimmering border (shimmer_bands bands of rainbow light running round the frame every shimmer_seconds), a spark running round the rim, lots of sparkles, and light rays turning slowly behind the animal (rays of them, ray_seconds a turn). Counts ending in _grid are the lighter version on cards in a big grid (Your Deck, the bans, the Animals tab, a match's army row), which also redraw only grid_fps times a second; everywhere else (offers, picks, cage openings, single cards) gets the full show. Cards only move while on screen. moment: when a Mythic is offered or picked, or freed from a cage: a white flash over the card (flash_alpha, fading over flash_seconds) with a pink ring bursting out to ring times the card's size (ring_width thick), a burst of sparkles and stars, a pop to pop_scale and a sound.

info._note: Holding a card anywhere (picking, offers, army row, deck, bans, collection), or an animal on the battlefield, shows its info popup near the finger (scripts/autoload/hold_info.gd, scripts/ui/info_pop.gd) for as long as it's held; the fight never pauses. hold_seconds: how long a hold takes; move_pixels: moving further than this is a drag (scrolling), not a hold. size: the popup's [width, height] in game pixels; gap: how far it sits from the finger. pop_seconds: its quick pop. The four bars compare the animal with the strongest in the game (at its level): Health and Damage are its whole squad's (on a square-root scale, so everyday animals don't look empty beside a Mythic hero); Speed: speed_bars for each speed; Range: its reach in tiles over range_full_tiles.

elements._note: The element looks every attack and ability effect is built from (docs/ART_DIRECTION.md, effects; fx_layer.gd "blast" and "linger", battle_field.gd _blast). An impact has three phases: the build-up on the animal (style_look.gd, gathering the element's particles onto it), the impact in layers (a white-hot core flash, the element's glow swelling, a shockwave ring racing out, the element's bits flying out of it: shards, flames, leaves, rocks, drops, stars, wisps, streaks, bolts, sparks; with its particles), and the fade ("linger": a stain of the glow on the ground with a few bits settled in it, flickering out over linger_seconds). Each element: core, glow and dark colors, its bits and its particle. style_elements: the element of each attack style (styles.json kinds); plain hits use "impact". A Mythic's big burst (blast_bits_big bits, blast_rings_big rings, blast_seconds_big long, a blast_shake shake) against a normal one (blast_bits, blast_seconds). In a crowded fight bits are halved (fx_layer crowded).
